moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
learningObjectives: Navigate the Testim visual editor and Test List to create, organize, and run tests.
Understand the role of the base URL and the AUT browser when recording and running a test.
Add basic validations to a recorded test so it checks outcomes, not just performs actions.
Run tests locally from the editor and from the Test List, and interpret the resulting pass/fail output.

elements.description: Testim's visual test editor has features built directly into the UI so that customizing a test — reordering steps, editing properties, adding validations — does not require writing code, while still allowing custom JavaScript steps for advanced cases (covered later in this learning path).

The project default base URL initializes new tests; an individual test can use another URL. It is the starting AUT address, not the editor address. For target editing, open the AUT and reach the relevant test state; opening only the initial page may not expose a later target.

bulletPoints: The editor is codeless-first: most editing is done through the UI, not code.
The base URL is where the AUT browser starts for both recording and running.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Running tests: editor vs. Test List

elements.description: The editor runs the open test locally or on a configured remote grid. Use the Play dropdown for Run on grid and choose the applicable configuration. Local editor playback uses Chrome; a single grid run is distinct from a cross-browser matrix.

One or more tests can be selected in the Test List (Ctrl/Cmd-click for multiple) and run together with the Play button. Tests run this way execute locally, which is useful for quickly re-checking a batch of related tests without leaving the Test List view.

elements.text: Local web playback uses Chrome. The editor also supports a single remote grid run. Use the documented CLI or Scheduler workflow for a cross-browser matrix with suitable grid configurations.

bulletPoints: Editor playback supports local Chrome or a configured remote grid run.
Test List local batch playback uses Chrome.
CLI/Scheduler workflows provide configured cross-browser matrix execution.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: From actions to assertions: basic validations

elements.description: Successful action replay establishes that those steps executed, not every business outcome or overall application health. Add assertions at meaningful outcomes; a click-through recording alone does not establish correctness.

Visible checks element existence and visibility, not its specific content. Text checks the chosen element’s expected content and supports Regex in Expected Value. The documented not-visible step is web-only: it asserts absence from view, not necessarily removal from the DOM.

elements.title: Adding a validation step
items: Reach the relevant AUT state, using a breakpoint and playback when needed.
At the insertion arrow, open predefined steps (M), then Validations.
Select the supported validation and target; set expected text where applicable, remove the breakpoint and run to check the result.

bulletPoints: Replay success does not establish all business outcomes.
Visibility, text and web-only not-visible checks assert different properties.
Expected Value supports Regex; choose matching criteria for the required outcome.

examPitfalls.title: Shipping a test with no validation steps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Recording a click-through flow and calling it 'done' because it runs without errors.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A test without validations only confirms the recording replays — it doesn't confirm the application produced the correct result. Add Validate element visible/text/not visible steps at the points that actually matter.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting a Test List run to cover cross-browser coverage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming that running tests from the Test List exercises multiple browsers automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Test List local runs use Chrome. The editor can also run a single test on a configured grid; CLI/Scheduler provide the documented cross-browser matrix workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the purpose of a project's base URL in Testim?

options.text: It is only used for licensing and has no effect on test recording or running.
It is the starting address the AUT browser opens before recording or running a test.
It is the URL of the Testim editor itself.
It is a placeholder that must always be left blank.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what the AUT browser needs before it can record or run anything.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The project default initializes the starting AUT URL for new tests; individual tests can override it. Target editing also requires the relevant application state, which may need playback beyond the starting page.

optionExplanations.A: The base URL directs the AUT, not licensing alone.
optionExplanations.B: It defines the starting AUT address; individual tests may override the project default.
optionExplanations.C: It is the application address, not the visual editor address.
optionExplanations.D: A usable application starting URL is needed for the recording workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A recorded test clicks through a checkout flow without throwing any errors, but does not confirm the order confirmation message actually appeared. What is missing?

options.text: Nothing — a test that runs without errors is complete.
A validation step, such as Validate element text, asserting the confirmation message's content.
A Reassign on the checkout button.

practiceQuiz.hint: Action replay alone does not assert the required confirmation content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Add a text assertion for the expected confirmation message. Successful replay alone does not establish that business outcome; target reassignment or CLI setup does not supply the missing assertion.

optionExplanations.A: Replay without the required outcome assertion is incomplete coverage.
optionExplanations.B: Text validation asserts the required confirmation content.
optionExplanations.C: Reassign changes the target; it does not assert the confirmation message.
optionExplanations.D: CLI configuration does not itself add the missing content assertion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which browser(s) can a test run on when triggered locally from the Test List?

options.text: Any browser installed on the machine, selected at run time.
Whichever browser was used during recording.

practiceQuiz.hint: The question specifies local Test List playback, not an editor grid run.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented local Test List batch workflow uses Chrome. The editor supports a separate single grid run, while CLI/Scheduler workflows provide cross-browser matrix execution.

optionExplanations.A: Local Test List playback does not select any installed browser.
optionExplanations.B: The documented local batch workflow runs in Chrome.
optionExplanations.C: Firefox/Safari grid configurations are not this local batch workflow.
optionExplanations.D: The local playback browser is not determined by the recording browser.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the 'Validate element text' step let you check that 'Validate element visible' does not?

options.text: Whether the element exists in the DOM at all.
That a specific text value appears within the specified element, optionally matched with Regex.
Whether the element has disappeared from the page.

practiceQuiz.hint: Visibility does not validate the element’s specific text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Text validation checks the required content of a chosen element and permits Regex matching. Visible validates existence and visibility without checking that content; not-visible and CSS checks assert different properties.

optionExplanations.A: Visible already checks element existence and visibility.
optionExplanations.B: Text validation checks the chosen element’s content, including supported Regex criteria.
optionExplanations.C: Absence from view is a not-visible check, not the added text assertion.
optionExplanations.D: A CSS-class assertion is a different validation.

quickRecap.value: Project defaults initialize new tests; individual URLs can differ. Reach the relevant AUT state for target editing.
Run the open test locally in Chrome or on a configured remote grid.
Selected web tests can run locally as a Chrome batch.
A single editor grid run is supported; CLI/Scheduler provide cross-browser matrix workflows.
Visible asserts existence and visibility; text asserts content; documented not-visible is web-only.
